Hi Alice —

Thanks for the invite and the packet. Quick answers to get us moving:

Portal steward: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> (I will be the primary steward for the initial intake).
Secondary steward (technical uploads): Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>.

Presign / temp creds: We prefer to use short-lived presign URLs for bulk evidence uploads. Typical pattern we use: presign TTL = 2 hours for initial staging, 24 hours max for one-off support uploads. If Brightleaf needs a longer TTL for large bulk transfers we can provide staged multipart uploads via a signed-bucket approach, but that requires a one-time ACL mapping.

Evidence naming: we attach a small checklist we use internally with the naming convention and manifest example — see attached redwood-portal-onboarding-checklist.xlsx. We generally include: <company>-<artifact>-<date>-<claim-id>.pdf and a manifest.csv with SHA256.

Open question for you: Does Brightleaf accept a single CAIQ mapping doc (we can produce a CAIQ-derived spreadsheet) or do you prefer per-question attachments? Also, on the presign side, do you enforce object-key prefix restrictions (we can match prefix redwood/onboarding/brightleaf/ if required).

If it helps, we can do a 20-minute run-through tomorrow to show the manifest + presign flow.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Vendor Security Intake | Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 10:05 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> ...

Couple of technical notes from our side (to make the presign + manifest handoff smoother):

1) Presign policy snippets (attached): we can emit presign URLs that are single-use and expire after the TTL you choose. For staging jobs that upload >2GB we recommend multipart + ephemeral creds; for small batches presign is fine.

2) Object-key prefix: we can lock uploads to a strict prefix (redwood/onboarding/brightleaf/<account-id>/). If you require signed headers (e.g., x-amz-meta-evidence-hash) we can add those to our upload flow.

3) Manifest format: CSV columns we will supply: object_key, original_filename, sha256_hex, uploader, upload_timestamp, claim_id. We will also post a sha256 manifest hash to a signed webhook once upload completes.

4) SOC2 note: if Brightleaf wants an out-of-band claim (evidence that is too large for the portal) we can provide a short-lived read-only bucket link and audit logs.

Attaching a small text file with the presign snippets — this contains example AWS CLI calls and the small IAM policy bits needed if you choose an upload role model.

Cheers,
Priyom
Security Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference

I scheduled a short 20-minute call to iron out the ACL/manifest webhook details — https://calendly.com/alice-spencer/30min (I booked the 10:30 slot). If you prefer to send the CAIQ mapping spreadsheet first, that works too — otherwise we'll capture answers directly in the portal.
